operating_rules: Quality of light source (hard vs soft light) fundamentally shapes contrast and emotion in photos
Strength of light source: strong = hard contrasty light; weak = soft diffused light
Direction of light source has the biggest impact on image; three main directions: front light (even exposure), side light (depth + interest), back light (dramatic + deep shadows)
Dynamic range limit: cameras capture 13-15 stops vs human eye 21-24 stops; strong light sources exceed camera latitude
Golden hour (sunrise/sunset) produces soft directional side light with depth and lower contrast
Blue hour (1hr before sunrise, 1hr after sunset) has soft light with blue tint; shoot at f1.4 or wider
Midday light is not inherently bad; hard light in cities creates strong geometric lines and leading shadows; avoid in foliage (creates hot spots)
Overcast/cloudy days diffuse sunlight into even, soft, beautiful light; ideal for portraits (even exposure across face)
Light modifiers shape hardness/softness/direction: soft boxes, 5-in-1 reflectors, diffusion sheets, smoke/haze/mist
White reflective surfaces bounce soft beautiful light; dark/black surfaces absorb light and enhance shadows
For headshots: keep subject head-and-shoulders straight on at first to simplify lighting tweaks
Jawline technique (turtle move): have subject bring neck forward and tilt chin slightly down; sharpens jaw for all body types
Never say 'smile' or 'say cheese'; instead make subject comfortable, talk naturally, disarm nervousness
Project confidence as photographer even if internally uncertain; maintain monitor angle so subject cannot see screen until review
Show client the process upfront (tethered shooting, periodic review) to build investment and establish expertise
named_methods: Split lighting (light at 9 or 3 o'clock: one side lit, other in shadow)
Rim lighting/Back light (light at 12 o'clock behind subject; pose in profile with black foam board between subject and light)
Butterfly lighting (light slightly above and in front at 6 o'clock; shadow under nose resembles butterfly)
Clamshell lighting (butterfly + reflector/fill light underneath; flatters by filling wrinkles)
Loop lighting (main light above eye level at ~5 or 7 o'clock; subtle shadows on one side of nose)
Rembrandt lighting (light at 4 or 8 o'clock; shadow from nose extends to cheekbone shadow; upside-down triangle light patch under eye)
Short lighting (Rembrandt position + subject turned toward light; slimming effect)
Broad lighting (Rembrandt position + subject turned away from light; makes face appear wider)
Cross lighting (main at 4-5 o'clock + edge light at 10-11 o'clock; dramatic 3D look)
Headshot positioning: start head-and-shoulders straight-on to simplify lighting and allow client familiarity
Turtle move (jawline technique): neck forward + chin down slightly to sharpen and define jawline
numbers: Dynamic range: cameras 13-15 stops vs human eye 21-24 stops
Blue hour: approximately 1 hour before sunrise and 1 hour after sunset
Headshot aperture at blue hour: f1.4 or wider
Clock model: camera at 6, model at center, hours represent light positions around face
specific_tactics: Use Photo Pills app to predict sun position for landscape shoots; know light angle in advance
Light positioning via clock model: visualize camera at 6 o'clock, model center, light hours around face
Catch light trick for rim lighting: have subject in profile facing left, turn head slightly toward light, shift camera left to capture silhouette with light on eyelids
Model light lowering: if butterfly creates dark eye socket shadows, turn on modeling light and lower modifier until catch light visible in pupils
Natural light only discussion: segment on artificial light deferred; prioritize sun, clouds, golden hour, blue hour for current context
Client comfort flow: greet + chat (common ground, industry talk) -> show monitor + explain tethered process -> build expertise perception -> minimize commands ('smile', 'relax')
Communication during shoots: continuous natural conversation (sports, family, job) to make subject forget camera presence
Monitor angle discipline: position monitor so subject cannot see it until intentional review moment
tools: Photo Pills (app for predicting sun position in landscape photography)
Milanote (project planning + mood board creation + collaboration; templates for photography/videography)
5-in-1 reflector set (reflect light, diffuse light via white sheet)
Black foam board (positioning between subject and rim light; used for silhouette setup)
Black cards/black boards (studio tool to enhance shadows in specific image areas)
Soft box (artificial light modifier to soften hardness)
Modeling light (studio flash feature; helps dial modifier height for catch light)
